_what: Synthetic Ruby bare-read gate for #3880 (RUBY-04), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, with ratios as the only timing gates. Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Ruby ScopeResolver and manifest loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a method misses an expected CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. blocks: small 128 methods x depth 4, methods 512 x 4, depth 128 x 16. heredocs: small 64 methods x 2 heredocs per opener line x 2 reads per body, methods 256 x 2 x 2, per_line 64 x 8 x 2, size 64 x 2 x 8. One class per file. Expected edges are computed from the source: every bare `target` that reads the parameter (in a block at any depth, or in a heredoc body) gets no edge; `helper` and `other(...)` stay calls; `other(<<~EOS, target = 1)` keeps the body's `target` as a call (the opener rule). main turns the parameter reads into wrong `Host<i>#target` edges (16 wrong at 16 x 4 blocks, 8 at 8 heredoc methods), so this gate fails without #3880.
_fingerprint_note: Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason, file, name, position).
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_4n/t_n)/4: about 1 is linear, about 4 is quadratic. 1.5 (bench/scope-capture) on every ratio: main is linear along these axes.
_depth_note: Not gated at these sizes: the climb from each bare read to its method is O(depth), so a nest where every level reads the parameter costs O(depth^2) in capture. Over depth 4 -> 64 the capture exponent is 1.50 (1.35-1.66) with #3880 against 1.18 (1.06-1.30) on main, 3.8-3.9x per doubling from depth 16 up (6288 vs 2342 ms at depth 64 x 128 methods). The gated depth range (4 -> 16) measures about 1.22.
_one_file_note: Not gated: on main, Ruby resolution is super-linear in the number of classes or methods in ONE file. With every class in one file (`--shape crowded`), 128 -> 1024 classes, resolution's fitted exponent is 1.39 (1.33-1.45) on main and 1.60 (1.49-1.72) with #3880; #3880 does not change resolution code, so the gated shapes use one class per file.
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.
_negative_controls_note: Building each scope's binding index without the per-file cache and through nested scopes (a temporary edit of rubyScopeBindings / forEachRubyScopeBinding in languages/ruby/captures.ts) fails blocks_capture_depth_scaling_ratio 3.527 > 1.5 in the CI profile, with unchanged fingerprints. Dropping the cache alone gave 1.436 (1.533 under the full protocol): below what the gate resolves reliably. These are deliberate regressions, not baseline observations.

Scalar ratios and millisecond values are per-metric maxima across the runs of that profile (rounded). peak_rss_mib (--full only) is each --shape child's high-water mark after one worker parse and one resolution, worker thread included; context, not gated.
